title: Inner product of two ±1 embeddings
statement:
For any two binary words $x, y$ of length $n$, let $\phi(x), \phi(y) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be their $\pm 1$ embeddings, whose $i$-th coordinates are $-1$ when the corresponding bit is true and $+1$ otherwise. Then their Euclidean inner product is
\[
\langle \phi(x),\, \phi(y)\rangle \;=\; n - 2\,d(x,y),
\]
where $d(x,y)$ is the Hamming distance, the number of coordinates on which $x$ and $y$ differ.
hypotheses_covered: x and y are binary words of length n
replaced:
For all binary words $x,y$ of length $n$,
\[
\langle \mathrm{pmOne}(x), \mathrm{pmOne}(y)\rangle \;=\; n - 2\,\mathrm{hdist}(x,y).
\]
